newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tuan Sing has no immediate plans to sell SPP stake.
newsitem.headline: Tuan Sing has no immediate plans to sell SPP stake.

text.p: Diversified property group Tuan Sing Holdings Ltd has no immediate plans to sell its stake in its construction arm, SPP Ltd, said Tuan Sing's chief executive officer and managing director Hwang Soo Chin on Monday.
"Right now we have not really considered disposing our stake" in SPP, Hwang told reporters after the ground breaking ceremony of KingsVille, a new property project in central Singapore.
But he said Tuan Sing could consider selling its stake later if the price and timing were right.
Hwang said Tuan Sing had not approached, or been approached by, anyone to sell its 62 percent stake in SPP.
Tuan Sing has traded actively on the Stock Exchange of Singapore in the past on rumours that it might be selling its stake in SPP.
Hwang said SPP had been "productive" for Tuan Sing and had established joint venture projects in the Philippines, Thailand, Burma, among other Asian countries.
"In 1997 we expect the (construction) group to show some results from some of these strategic alliances," he said.
This was despite "margins being under slight pressure" due to a late start in its government-subsidised housing projects in Singapore.
Construction constributed about 20 percent of profit before tax to Tuan Sing in 1995.

Hwang said Tuan Sing was aiming for an equal 30 percent contribution from property, construction, and manufacturing and 10 percent from trading. The bulk of its earnings now comes from its property division, he said.
